main_positive_finding: Full-validation-gated focused graph surgery reliably transfers local estimate upward in small increments and should be kept as a submission post-pass/calibration lane.
main_negative_finding: Fresh dynamic ONNX lowerings and artifact harvesting for task185/task365/task366 did not produce score-scale gains because selector/writeback/full-grid intermediate costs dominate.
root_cause_of_failure: The campaign improved only redundant existing artifacts, not the number of tasks solved by low-cost 250-600 class programs. LB 7500 requires hundreds of points of safe local delta, while this campaign added only 0.153 local.
next_research_direction_if_campaign_resu: Build a real NeuroGolf compiler IR with cost extraction before ONNX emission: infer shape/object programs in Python, lower only through proven low-cost primitives (one-node/fused data movement, small Slice/Gather/Pad, small local-mask Conv), and reject full-grid Where/GatherND/ScatterND/dynamic MatMul before candidate generation.
stop_condition: Reached campaign experiment 30; no further experiments should be run in this campaign without a new user instruction.
submission_decision: exp127 is a submit-safe calibration candidate after user review, but it is not an LB7500 candidate.
leakage_risk: low for accepted graph-surgery deltas; medium for future public-artifact-derived compiler priors unless transformed into explicit rules.
overfitting_risk: low-to-medium for repeated same-task graph surgery; high for any raw coordinate/key lookup compiler.
